sec: Wilson's genetics, Menkes, copper transport and acute presentation

items.q: What is the pattern of inheritance and genetic locus responsible for Wilson's disease?
opts: Autosomal recessive, caused by mutation in the ATP7B gene on chromosome 13q
Autosomal dominant, caused by mutation in the HFE gene on chromosome 6p
X-linked recessive, caused by mutation in the ATP7A gene on the X chromosome
Autosomal recessive, caused by mutation in the ABCC2 gene on chromosome 10q
items.exp: Wilson's disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by dysfunction of ATP7B (Wilson ATPase) located on chromosome 13q. (Book p1013)

items.q: Match each inherited disorder of copper transport with its gene and clinical presentation — 1) Wilson's disease 2) Menkes kinky hair disease … A) ATP7A on X chromosome, causing severe copper deficiency, seizures, hypotonia, and brittle hair at 3 months B) ATP7B on chromosome 13q, causing copper overload presenting between 3 to 20 years
items.exp: Wilson's is ATP7B on chr 13q presenting between 3–20 years; Menkes is ATP7A on the X chromosome causing copper deficiency with brittle hair and seizures at 3 months. (Book p1013)

items.q: What are the physiological quantities for daily ingestion of copper and its mucosal entry in the upper small bowel?
opts: Daily intake: 2–5 mg; Daily absorbed: approximately 1 mg
Daily intake: 10–15 mg; Daily absorbed: approximately 5 mg
Daily intake: 0.2–0.5 mg; Daily absorbed: approximately 0.1 mg
Daily intake: 20–30 mg; Daily absorbed: approximately 10 mg
items.exp: Daily copper intake is 2–5 mg, of which approximately 1 mg is absorbed mainly in the duodenum via DMT1. (Book p1013)

items.q: Which of the following foods is NOT listed as a copper-rich substance on this page?
items.exp: The three copper-rich substances listed are Chocolates, Nuts, and Mushrooms; citrus fruits are not listed. (Book p1013)

items.q: Fill up: Inside the duodenal mucosal cell, absorbed copper is sequestered by the intracellular protein ______.
items.exp: The enterocyte diagram labels: 'metallothionase [metallothionein] : Sequestors Cu inside cell'. (Book p1013)

items.q: Why is Wilson's disease clinically impossible to diagnose in an infant under 3 years of age?
opts: Intracellular metallothionein requires a minimum of 3 years to become saturated and depleted of binding capacity
ATP7B expression does not activate until puberty
Maternal ceruloplasmin persists in neonatal circulation for up to 36 months
Intestinal DMT1 does not absorb dietary copper during early childhood
items.exp: Metallothionein takes a minimum of 3 years to deplete its capacity, setting the minimum age of Wilson's presentation at 3–20 years. (Book p1013)

items.q: What is the fundamental molecular defect underlying ceruloplasmin abnormality in Wilson's disease?
opts: Failure to incorporate copper into apoceruloplasmin, leading to accelerated ceruloplasmin degradation
Total absence of apoceruloplasmin peptide synthesis by ribosomes
Excessive renal tubular excretion of intact ceruloplasmin
items.exp: The defect is: 'Cu2+ not being incorporated in ceruloplasmin (fundamental defect) -> ↓ Ceruloplasmin degradation'. (Book p1013)

items.q: What baseline physiological concentration is expected for circulating ceruloplasmin, and below what level is it diagnostic of hepatic copper retention?
items.exp: Normal serum ceruloplasmin is 20–35 mg/dL, whereas in Wilson's disease it is characteristically < 10 mg/dL. (Book p1013)

items.q: Assess the two statements on copper handling: I Excess systemic copper in healthy humans is cleared primarily via renal tubular filtration and enterohepatic recycling. II Apoceruloplasmin is a positive acute phase reactant and can appear falsely normal or elevated during systemic inflammation.
items.exp: Statement I is false because biliary excretion is the sole physiological route ('Nil renal/enterohepatic circulation'). Statement II is true because apoceruloplasmin is a positive acute phase reactant. (Book p1013)

items.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with acute jaundice, marked fatigue, and pallor. Laboratory testing reveals low hemoglobin with negative direct Coombs test, low cholinesterase, mildly elevated AST and ALT, and a paradoxically low serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP). What metabolic liver disease must be urgently suspected?
opts: Wilson's disease presenting as acute fulminant hepatitis
Acute Hepatitis A infection with severe cholestasis
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with panacinar emphysema
items.exp: Acute hepatitis in a patient <20 years with low Hb, low cholinesterase, mild transaminitis, and low ALP strongly indicates acute Wilson's disease. (Book p1013)

items.q: Which of the following findings is NOT part of the classic constellation that raises suspicion for acute Wilson's disease in an adolescent?
opts: Age < 20 years with unexplained fatty liver
Low serum cholinesterase with mild transaminitis
items.exp: Wilson's acute presentation features LOW alkaline phosphatase (due to zinc displacement by copper), not elevated ALP. (Book p1013)
